subject: Scaling scenarios and committed GPU headroom — Mosaic Health renewal
messages:
From: Alex Park <apark@mosaichealth.ai>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@mosaichealth.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — committed headroom ask

Hi Logan,

Renewal for Mosaic is coming up next quarter and we need to lock in committed GPU headroom for our production chat and triage pipelines. Usage has spiked over the last two months — attached is a short QPS/token forecast (Mosaic_QPS_forecast.xlsx) that shows two growth scenarios.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a recommended reserved GPU count (and breakout by model family) and an optional phased uplift approach so we don’t overcommit immediately? Also need throughput guarantees for our busiest window (US East peak 09:00-11:00PT).

Elena and I are available for a 30-min sizing call this week.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Park
Head of Platform
Mosaic Health

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — committed headroom ask

Hi Alex — thanks for the forecast. Looping in Marissa (AM) and Ben (SE) to validate assumptions and propose concrete sizing + contract options.

Quick asks from our side so recommendations map cleanly to contract terms:
- Baseline avg QPS today and 95th percentile peak QPS in a single AZ (if available)
- Typical request size (avg tokens in/out) and percent of requests hitting longest-context models vs small embedding models
- Any strict latency SLOs at 95th/99th percentile during peak windows

Ben — can you produce three headroom scenarios (Conservative, Expected, Aggressive) with recommended reserved GPU counts, preferred instance/shape, and notes on batching/kv cache configs we should include in the amendment?

Marissa — once Ben shares numbers, can you propose a term structure (phased uplift vs immediate commit) and a suggested discount ladder for the committed pool? Alex — we can follow with DocuSign/AM plan after we agree.

I’ve added a 30-min slot Thu 10:30 PT on the calendar — please confirm.

Best,
Logan Wright

On Sun, Aug 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Alex Park <apark@mosaichealth.ai> wrote:
> Renewal for Mosaic is coming up next quarter and we need to lock in committed GPU headroom...

Thanks — I ran the numbers against the forecast in Mosaic_QPS_forecast.xlsx. Quick summary of assumptions:
- Model mix: 65% medium generator (7B-class), 25% large chat (34–70B-class quantized), 10% embeddings/low-latency utility models.
- Avg request: 180 tokens in, 220 tokens out (avg total 400 tokens).
- Desired P95 latency target during peak: <= 350 ms per token generation step for medium generator; for large chat we recommend workload-specific SLOs (see notes).
- Batching: continuous batching with target batch sizes of 8–12 for medium models; 2–4 for large chat. KV cache hit rate assumed 60% for repeated contexts.

Scenario recommendations (reserved pool sizing, single-region US East):
1) Conservative (buffered): +8 A100-80GB equiv GPUs reserved (add to existing pool of 12 -> 20 total). Covers +35% QPS growth, maintains P95 targets with modest batching.
2) Expected (recommended): +16 A100-80GB equiv GPUs reserved (12 -> 28 total). Covers +85% QPS growth, handles large-chat bursts with dedicated subset (4 GPUs pinned to large-chat variants) and autoscale burst allowance of 4 GPUs.
3) Aggressive (growth-ready): +28 A100-80GB equiv GPUs reserved (12 -> 40 total). Covers 2x QPS growth, provides headroom for new feature rollouts and 99th-percentile protection.

Notes:
- Equivalent GPU counts assume mixed instance types; final amendment should reference effective GPU units rather than exact SKU to allow flexibility.
- Quantization: recommend int8+ approach for 34B/70B variants to reduce memory & increase throughput — improves effective throughput by ~1.6x vs fp16.
- Pricing: reserved pool pricing model supports step-up commitments (month 0–3 partial commit, full commit month 4). Will need Marissa to map to discount tiers.

Attachments: short sizing sheet included as 'Mosaic_QPS_forecast.xlsx' (row-level throughput sims).

Happy to walk through the simulation during the call.

—Ben

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Cc: Alex Park <apark@mosaichealth.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@mosaichealth.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — committed headroom ask

Thanks Ben — that gives a nice ladder to present. From an AM/contract perspective I’d propose two commercial paths:

Option A — Phased uplift (lower near-term commitment):
- 12-month term
- Month 0–3: 50% of expected reserved pool committed (soft-commit with 30-day notice to convert to full commit)
- Month 4+: remainder converts to full commit; 10% discount applied to committed pool vs list
- Add-on: guaranteed 4-GPU burst window for 30 minutes per peak hour included

Option B — Immediate full commit (better economics):
- 12-month term
- Full Expected scenario committed (16 GPU uplift)
- 20% discount on committed monthly charge, $0.00 setup for reserved pool changes during term
- SLA: P99 latency fallback policy + $X credit per incident (standard enterprise SLA)

Thoughts: Option A reduces upfront spend and gives Mosaic operational runway; Option B is cleaner for forecasting and provides meaningful unit-cost savings. We can also structure a 9-month ramp (50% -> 100% over 3 months) if regulatory procurement prefers shorter lock-ins.

I’ll prepare a proposed amendment (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf) reflecting both options, with clear upgrade triggers tied to QPS thresholds.

Marissa Cole
Account Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Alex Park <apark@mosaichealth.ai>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, Elena Torres <elena.torres@mosaichealth.ai>
Date: 2027-08-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — committed headroom ask

Logan/Marissa/Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifying points from our procurement/security side:
- We prefer the phased uplift (Option A) but need a firm conversion trigger (e.g., sustained P95 > 220 QPS for 7 consecutive days) rather than a time-based auto-convert.
- Can you confirm the recommended reserved GPUs will be isolated to our VPC/dedicated routing (no multi-tenant noisy neighbor risk)?
- For pricing, can we see both monthly committed charge and effective per-token cost at 50% vs 100% commit?

If you can update the amendment with the trigger language and per-token cost table, we can route for legal review and issue a PO. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Alex Park <apark@mosaichealth.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, Elena Torres <elena.torres@mosaichealth.ai>

Subject: Final: Renewal uplift path & next steps (Mosaic Health)

Alex — updating after internal sync:
Action items we’ll deliver by EOD tomorrow:
- Marissa: proposed_amendment_v2.pdf updated with an explicit conversion trigger: sustained P95 > 220 QPS for 7 consecutive days OR manual conversion request from Mosaic procurement (whichever comes first). Also includes both commercial Option A (phased) and Option B (full commit) with per-token cost tables for 50% and 100% commit.
- Ben: a short technical appendix included in the amendment describing reserved pool isolation, pinning policy for large-chat GPUs, and expected P95/P99 latency ranges under each scenario.
- Legal/Finance: we’ll attach a draft DocuSign link for PO signature once Mosaic confirms Option A vs B.

Tentative timeline: sign by Aug 31 to hit new reserved capacity by Oct 1. If you want the full-aggressive uplift earlier, we can expedite but need purchase order confirmation.

Thanks everyone — will send updated docs shortly.

Best,
